title: Punt ST: Player Targets
brief: Which players fit a punt ST build, and what do they bring in the stable categories? It must explain that steals are among the most variable categories, so they are a sensible punt and a risky thing to pay for.
summary: Steals vary more than almost any other category, both from game to game and from season to season. That makes them a sensible punt and a bad place to spend auction money. In our league, spend the 200 USD on stable categories like points and assists. Fill the last roster spots with 1 to 2 USD centers who add blocks, rebounds and FG% but almost no steals, led by Khaman Maluach and Yves Missi.

sections.heading: Why steals are a sensible punt

paragraphs.text: Steals swing a lot from game to game and from season to season. Even elite steals players can drop to 0.7 or 0.8 per game in a down year. One expert names steals and FT% as the two categories that change most from year to year.

High-variance categories are the better ones to punt. Even with no steals specialists, you will still win the category some weeks by luck. That softens the cost of punting it in a 9-category head-to-head matchup.
Steals do not tie strongly to either the guard build or the big man build. So punting steals fits with either one. You do not have to commit to a style before the draft.

sections.heading: Why paying for steals is risky

paragraphs.text: Steals are low volume and very variable. One expert ranks them lower for that reason and says not to rely on them. A player whose value depends on steals carries extra risk. If most of a player's value comes from steals, do not pay full price for him in our 18 October auction.
Steals also cause oddities in standard 9-cat rankings. Before you bid, look at what a player's ranking rests on. If steals are holding up his ranking, value him lower than his Yahoo rank suggests.

The notes do not disagree about steals being variable. They point to two uses for that fact. One view is to punt steals outright, because they are high-variance. The other is that steals are among the most common categories on the waiver wire. So a manager who changes his mind in season can add steals with FAB, within the 6 adds per week, instead of buying them on draft day. Either way, the auction is the wrong place to pay for them.

Points and assists are stable, high-volume categories, and they are bad to punt. In a punt ST build, spend the main share of the 200 USD on players who produce points and assists. Don't spend it on steals.

All the punt ST fits in our data are centers or bigs priced at 0 to 2 USD. They do not supply the points and assists. What they add is rebounds, blocks, FG% and, in a few cases, some threes. Buy them at the end of the auction to round out the build after the main spending is done.

Khaman Maluach is the best late target. His blocks are a real outlier, and he adds rebounds and FG% with about 0.4 steals projected. Phoenix's 4-4-4 playoff schedule adds late value. Pay 1 to 2 USD near the 144-player cutoff.
Yves Missi is a 1 to 2 USD center for blocks and FG%. Yahoo projects 61.6% FG and ESPN 54.5%. He fits teams punting steals or threes.

Nikola Vučević gets very few steals for a center. He fits a punt ST build that wants rebounds and some threes from the center spot. He is now Wendell Carter Jr.'s backup, so treat him as a 1 USD flyer and Carter handcuff, not a starter. His 8.6 to 13.8 point range depends on whether he gets about 25 minutes.

Aaron Gordon fits punt ST with about 52% FG projected and few turnovers. He played only 36 games last season and has had repeated hamstring and calf problems. Pay 1 USD at most or leave him for waivers.

Isaiah Stewart, Brook Lopez and Ryan Kalkbrenner fit punt ST but should not be drafted. Stewart projects about 1.6 blocks on 54% shooting with about 0.3 steals, but only matters when Edey is out. Lopez could give blocks and threes with about 0.5 steals if he ever reaches about 30 minutes. Kalkbrenner blocked 1.5 shots in 21.4 minutes last season, but experts expect him to be Charlotte's last center. Add them with FAB only if their role grows.

In the first weeks, check minutes for the bigs you drafted. Maluach needs about 24 minutes and the starting job over Ighodaro. Missi needs to start over Derik Queen at about 25 minutes. Vučević needs to beat 15 to 20 minutes against Carter and Bitadze. Drop any of them quickly if the minutes do not come, and use the spot on a waiver pickup.
